correctness.rationale: The two order-24 extensions differ by the quadratic character. Square/nonsquare projection gives half the sum and difference of their Gauss sums; the scaled determinant is their nonzero product and a surviving entry has modulus p. The Jacobi–Gauss identity makes the zero condition J=±p. For t a unit mod 24 and b the positive residue of pt, the two digits of (p²−1)t/24 are (pt−b)/24 and (bp−t)/24, so Stickelberger yields the asserted normalized valuation (up to uniform sign convention). The residues 13,17,19,23 give equal valuations for the pair t,t+12 at every conjugate prime, so J/p is integral; it has unit modulus in every embedding. Inversion fixes J under ζ24→ζ24^11, and among roots of unity in this cyclotomic field only ±1 are fixed. In the other four classes t=1 and t=13 have different valuations and cyclotomic conjugacy transfers the obstruction to all extensions. The subfield restrictions for 17 and 19 indeed have orders 4 and 6, and Frobenius does not swap extensions in these classes. Independently evaluated the compressed Fourier zeros directly in the cyclotomic coefficient basis at 20 primes and all four characters per prime (python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_reviews.py 1); it does not use the supplied checker's Jacobi-sum enumeration and does not replace the valuation proof.
